sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer and TSL cel materials with WebGL 2 compatibility fallback; Rapier 3D 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; WebRTC; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; single HTML with CDN library dependencies
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel shading, ink outlines, layered low-poly jungle diorama and a torchlit underground route
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and NumberKeyframeTrack character rigs; procedural pendulum, wildlife and environment motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-synthesized marimba-style music, percussion, jungle chirps, sound effects and formant-filtered Animalese-style gibberish; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1 host-authoritative shared-world co-op for 1–4; standalone WebRTC direct co-op for 2; same-browser BroadcastChannel co-op for 2; couch co-op for 1–4. WebRTC was verified between two local browser pages; connectivity across unrelated Internet networks is unknown.
sourceInformation.testing: 45/45 checks passed. Headless Chromium software WebGPU and file:// startup; scripted full controller playthrough with invulnerability and no developer travel; Rapier traversal and hazards; UI, gamepad stub, multitouch and offline audio synthesis; two-page WebRTC co-op; official AI Hub 2/4-player, 150 ms latency / 50 ms jitter / 5% loss, host-leave and dedicated-server harness cases. TV visuals reviewed at 1920x1080 through WebGL 2 because headless WebGPU screenshots can be blank. Physical controllers, real mobile devices and cross-network Internet connectivity: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none; only the user-supplied AI Hub integration and pinned dependency source files were retrieved

testingFeedback: 5 observed game issues were fixed: co-op roster removal, early rendering delaying Hub readiness, foreground art obscuring the scout, decorative arrows leaking into accessible button labels, and couch camera framing across surface and cave levels. Test-driver corrections and transient software-GPU resource failures are excluded.

2 were game breaking in the tested conditions: a departing scout cleared the remaining co-op roster and invalidated the result; an early software-WebGPU draw could delay four-player Hub readiness past its deadline.

The official four-player AI Hub harness with 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter and 5% loss exposed the co-op failures. The continuous controller bot then completed all six treasures and the final gate with normal collision, 24 jumps, 7 vine catches and no rescues; only invulnerability was enabled.
The initial native WebGPU screenshot was blank on the headless software adapter and could not verify the art. WebGL 2 compatibility screenshots were useful for visual review.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL materials and AnimationMixer made a consistent procedural cel-and-ink style and expressive reusable character clips possible without external art.

I initially guessed the Rapier module filename incorrectly and corrected it from the pinned package manifest. Software-WebGPU startup and blank screenshots required separating the session handshake from the first draw and using the compatibility backend for visual review.
The platform controller, vine and ladder traversal, authored jungle route, controller-first menus, shared-world networking and procedural music, effects and gibberish voices.
Coordinating fixed-step Rapier bodies, sensor-based traversal, native animation transitions and authoritative network snapshots while handling WebGPU initialization correctly.
none; Three.js, Rapier and the bundled AI Hub session client are unmodified.
A built-in fixed-step character-controller and interpolation layer with explicit animation-state hooks and clearer WebGPU initialization failure paths.
promptFeedback: The specific source, controller-first philosophy, procedural audio rule, attract mode and live tuning requirement provided a clear target for a complete vertical slice.
Research was prohibited while a linked multiplayer protocol was required. I treated the supplied protocol and pinned dependency files as implementation inputs, not game-design research.
Completing a single-file platform adventure with native WebGPU visuals, physics traversal, standalone co-op, Hub synchronization and a continuous automated playthrough.
Clarify whether standalone multiplayer must work across unrelated Internet networks, and explicitly allow required protocol/dependency downloads when game-design research is prohibited.

aiHub.name: Pit & Run
aiHub.tagline: Six treasures. One sunset. Still got the hat.
aiHub.description: Swing through an inked jungle, time crocodile smiles and brave torchlit shortcuts to recover six lost treasures. Explore solo or share the expedition with up to four scouts.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or left stick: move; Space/Cross/A: jump and release vine; E/Square/X or up/down: grab and climb; Esc/Options: pause; touch: drag left, tap right.
